supportBackup.title: Create support backup
supportBackup.howItWorks: This produces a de-identified copy of your backup: names are masked (first and last two characters kept), notes/descriptions/account numbers are removed, and every amount is multiplied by a single hidden factor while public values (exchange rates, prices, interest rates) are left intact. The file is always encrypted with the password below and restores like a normal backup. This protects against casual exposure, not against someone who already knows you -- dates, frequencies and structure are preserved so bugs still reproduce.
supportBackup.priceHistoryHint: Off by default: a full price series matches public market data and can identify a masked ticker. Turn on only when the bug concerns prices or valuations.
supportBackup.accountsHint: Leave all unchecked to include every account. Picking a subset also pulls in the accounts and payees they reference.
supportBackup.dateRangeHint: Limit exported history to these dates. Opening balances are adjusted so the trimmed file still reconciles.
supportBackup.multiplierHint: Every private amount is multiplied by this number to hide the actual value while keeping everything consistent. Any non-integer greater than 1 works; Regenerate picks a new one.
supportBackup.multiplierWarning: Do not share the multiplier with anyone — it is the key that reverses the hidden amounts.
supportBackup.previewEmpty: No sample rows to preview for this selection.
supportBackup.previewFailed: Could not build the preview. Please try again.
supportBackup.confirmPasswordMessage: The file can only be opened with the encryption password shown above. It is not stored anywhere and cannot be recovered later -- make sure you saved it before generating.
supportBackup.generateFailed: Could not generate the support backup. Please try again.
supportBackup.passwordHint: The file is always encrypted. Share this password with the investigator through a separate channel, not alongside the file.

help.whatIsBody: Enable Banking is a company that is licensed in the EU as an account information service provider (AISP) under PSD2. It connects to your bank for you and gives Monize read-only access to your accounts, balances and transactions. You sign in at your own bank. Monize and Enable Banking never see your bank password. Enable Banking works with banks in the European Economic Area.
help.dataFlow: After you connect your bank, Enable Banking can read your bank data: your account data passes through its service on the way to Monize. Enable Banking states that it does not store this data. Its terms apply: <terms>Enable Banking API terms</terms>.
help.whatIsFree: For personal use, a free application in restricted production mode is enough. It reads only the accounts that you link to it in the control panel.
help.step1: Create an account at <link>Enable Banking</link> (select "Get Started" and wait for the confirmation email). Then sign in to the control panel and open "API applications".
help.step2: Select "Production". Monize reads your real bank accounts only through a Production application. Select "Sandbox" only if you want to try the connection first: it shows only demo data from test banks.
help.step3: Keep "Generate in the browser" for the private key.
help.step4: Enter the values below in the form. For "Production", every field is required.
help.registrationValuesTitle: Values to paste into the form
help.registrationValuesNote: The labels and values stay in English because the control panel is in English.
help.registrationTemplatesNote: The two URLs point to the Monize templates. In restricted mode Enable Banking does not check them. If other people use your Monize instance, publish your own pages with your name instead.
help.step5: Select "Register". Your browser saves the private key file (.pem). Keep this file secret.
help.step6: For "Production", the new application shows "Inactive". Select "Activate by linking accounts", select the country, your bank and the usage type ("personal" for a personal account, "business" for a company account), and select "Link". Then sign in at your bank and authorize your accounts. Do not select "Request activation": it asks for general availability, which personal use does not need. Without linked accounts the bank returns no accounts. Later, when you connect the bank in Monize, select the same usage type.
help.step7: Enter the application ID from the application list, and load the private key file here.
help.sandboxNote: Transactions from a Sandbox application are demo data. Link a Sandbox bank account only to a test account in Monize, not to an account that holds your real transactions.
help.networkBody: When the bank sends you back, your browser opens the redirect URL. Enable Banking servers do not connect to Monize. Thus Monize does not have to be reachable from the internet or from Enable Banking IP addresses. The redirect URL must open in the browser that you use to authorize access.
help.networkOutbound: The Monize server must be able to connect to api.enablebanking.com over HTTPS (port 443).

connect.title: Connect a bank

connect.whySecondAuthorization: You authorize at your bank again here, even if you already linked the same accounts in the Enable Banking control panel. The control panel only lists which accounts the application may read, and its consent ends the same day. This step gives Monize its own consent to read balances and transactions, for up to 180 days. When it is about to end, the connection card shows "Renew consent".
